Review done. PR #1930 clean, small. 3 findings, all low-severity:

**1. Broad discovery on `add`/`remove` (agent_group.go:117)** — uses `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways`, scans all `$PATH`, execs `info` on every `entire-agent-*` binary even though target name known. Arbitrary-code-exec surface + shared 10s budget per add/remove. Fix: use `external.DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways(ctx, types.AgentName(name))` — short-circuits built-ins, execs only matching binary.

**2. Swallowed discovery errors (agent_group.go:117, same root cause)** — `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` returns nothing, so real plugin failure (`entire-agent-zed` errors/times out) shows as generic "Unknown agent" via `printWrongAgentError`. `DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways` returns the error → surface it.

**3. Test pollutes global registry (agent_group_test.go:86)** — `TestAgentGroup_DiscoversExternalAgents` leaks `ext-agentgroup-test` into process-global agent registry, factory points at temp binary deleted at cleanup. Later `cli` tests enumerating agents see phantom backed by nonexistent binary. Self-consistent today, latent flake, no reset seam.

Not bugs (verified clean): `add` correctly auto-persists `external_agents=true` (setup.go:1886), non-parallel test justified (`t.Setenv` on PATH).

Strongest action: #1/#2 same fix — swap to `DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways` for single-name commands, keep broad scan only for `list`. Author mirrored `entire enable`, but `enable --agent` shares same pre-existing inefficiency.

<result>Fixed the two substantive findings. Summary of what changed in `cmd/entire/cli/agent_group.go`:

**Findings 1 & 2 (same root cause) — fixed.** `add` and `remove` now call `external.DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways(ctx, types.AgentName(name))` instead of the broad `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways`. This:
- Executes only the single named `entire-agent-<name>` binary rather than shelling out to every `entire-agent-*` plugin on `$PATH` for a targeted command (and short-circuits instantly for built-ins, where `agent.Get` already succeeds).
- Surfaces the plugin's real load/timeout error (`loading external agent %q: ...`) instead of masking it behind the generic "unknown agent" message. `SilenceUsage` is set so the usage blob isn't dumped for a prerequisite failure.
- Preserves existing UX for a bogus name: lookup returns `ErrNotFound` → `nil`, then `agent.Get` fails → `printWrongAgentError` as before.

`list` deliberately keeps the broad `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` since it must enumerate every plugin.

**Finding 3 (test-isolation) — not changed, by design.** The global-registry leak comes from `runAgentList` running discovery (correct production behavior for a single-process CLI), and the pre-existing `TestRunAgentList_*` tests already trigger it. It stays self-consistent and benign; cleanly fixing it would require adding an `Unregister`/reset seam to the `agent` package purely for tests (the cli-package test can't reach the internal `registry` var), which isn't warranted for a low-severity, non-failing leak.

Verification:
- `go build ./cmd/entire/cli/` — clean
- `mise run fmt` — applied
- golangci-lint 2.11.3 (mise binary, direct) on `./cmd/entire/cli/...` — 0 issues
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/ -run 'TestAgentGroup_DiscoversExternalAgents|TestRunAgentList|TestAgentGroupBareCommand'` — PASS

Note: I did not run the full `mise run test:ci` (unit + integration + e2e canary) — worth running before you commit/push per the project checklist.</result>
